title: Function-level precedent can match the wrong callee when multiple functions share a name

finding.claim: Function-level precedent can match the wrong callee when multiple functions share a name
finding.evidence: The function-key builder indexes callees only by bare name, so later definitions overwrite earlier ones and call sites are matched to whichever same-named function was seen last. In a supported Python module with two different methods or nested functions sharing a name, a precedent for one enclosing function can be treated as still valid or invalid based on an unrelated same-named function elsewhe
finding.recommendation: Key callees by qualified name or by lexical scope instead of bare `n.name`, and resolve `ast.Attribute` calls against the enclosing class/function scope so same-named functions in other scopes cannot alias each other in the precedent hash.

refutation.reason: The finding claims that indexing callees by bare name causes later definitions to overwrite earlier ones, but the quoted line shows the code uses `setdefault`, which preserves the first value and does not overwrite existing entries.

probe.summary: Mechanism verified at HEAD during the inventory sweep (`by_name.setdefault` = first definition wins; nothing overwrites). Residue CONFIRMED by construction and now by test: two same-named functions, a caller of the second — the pre-fix key hashed the FIRST body, so changing the called function did not move the key. FAIL-SAFE FIX LANDED (commit c1bf1df): qualified resolution where determinable (self.x() → the enclosing class's method, unique scope-local sibling); an ambiguous bare name keys to ALL candidates' hashes; unambiguous names keep the historical bare hash, so existing precedents keep matching. Pinned in `tests/test_v111_hardening.py::CalleeKeyTests`; parent-fail verified (`hardening-parent-fail.txt`: ambiguous + self-call tests fail pre-fix, controls pass).
